name: rafeeq

scripts.ios:sync: npm run build:prod && npx cap sync ios
scripts.android:sync: npm run build:prod && npx cap sync android
scripts.android:build: npm run android:sync && cd android && set "JAVA_HOME=C:\Program Files\Android\Android Studio\jbr" && .\gradlew.bat assembleDebug bundleRelease
scripts.analyze: npm run build:prod -- --stats-json && npx webpack-bundle-analyzer build/stats.json

_ionic_pin_note: @ionic/react and @ionic/react-router are pinned to ~8.7 and ionicons to ~8.0: from @ionic/core 8.8.0 and ionicons 8.1.0 their Stencil type declarations use `const` type parameters, which TypeScript 4.9 (the version react-scripts 5 allows) cannot parse, so `tsc --noEmit` fails. Lift the pins together with a TypeScript 5 upgrade.
_browserslist_note: Floor is chrome 89 (Ionic 8's minimum; it was 79 under Ionic 7), not a market-share query. `>0.2%` resolved `and_chr` to the single LATEST Android Chrome, giving zero coverage of stale WebViews on old devices — WebView updates via Play independently of the OS, so the OS version says nothing about the engine. 89 = Ionic 8's supported minimum and the binding constraint; 79, the `max()` floor of the --safe-inset-* tokens, sits below it. Keep capacitor.config.ts android.minWebViewVersion in step. This governs JS SYNTAX transpilation only — newer CSS (color-mix, font-palette) is handled by per-declaration fallbacks and degrades gracefully, so do NOT raise this floor to match a CSS feature. See docs/webview-compat-audit.md.
